skill.name: design-spec-extraction
skill.description: Extract structured UI design specifications from user-provided Figma exports, screenshots, mockups, or website captures. The skill creates design tokens, component trees, layout data, and accessibility notes for developer handoff.
skill.summary: Extract design tokens and component specifications from visual UI sources.
skill.author: Cygnusfear

security_audit.summary: Most static findings are false positives caused by markdown code fences, inline design-spec paths, design grid terminology, and schema or documentation URLs. The screenshot references describe user-provided visual inputs, not covert capture or upload. Two mkdir examples are confirmed as limited command-use risks, and one semantic finding covers unsafe project-name substitution.

remediation.issue: Project names are substituted into output paths and bash examples without validation.
remediation.suggestion: Require a safe slug such as letters, numbers, and hyphens, and reject path separators or shell metacharacters before writing files.

remediation.issue: The workflow includes bash mkdir examples for creating local output directories.
remediation.suggestion: Prefer tool-mediated file creation or a fixed safe directory example, and avoid shell commands when they are not required.

remediation.issue: Screenshot inputs can contain confidential designs, credentials, or third-party UI material.
remediation.suggestion: State that images must be user-authorized and should not include secrets, private customer data, or restricted third-party content.

content.user_title: Extract UI Design Specs from Screenshots
content.value_statement: Manual design handoff from screenshots is slow and inconsistent. This skill extracts tokens, components, layout, and accessibility notes into structured design-spec files.
actual_capabilities: Extracts layout regions, grid systems, and bounding boxes from provided visual inputs.
Builds color, typography, spacing, sizing, border, radius, shadow, and transition tokens.
Produces six intermediate pass files and one final design-spec file under .design-specs.
Maps UI components into a hierarchy with variants, states, and accessibility metadata.
Checks contrast, focus indicators, touch targets, and ARIA recommendations.
Uses included schema and extraction pattern references for validation guidance.
limitations: Requires user-provided images, exports, or captures before analysis can begin.
Color values, spacing, and font names are estimates when only pixels are available.
Does not browse live websites or capture screens by itself.
Writes local output files and needs permission to create the .design-specs directory.

use_cases.title: Create Implementation Tokens
use_cases.description: Turn a provided UI screenshot into design tokens and component notes for frontend implementation.

use_cases.title: Document Existing Interfaces
use_cases.description: Extract reusable colors, type styles, spacing, and component patterns from approved product screens.

use_cases.title: Review Visual Accessibility
use_cases.description: Identify contrast issues, touch target concerns, focus states, and semantic structure from design images.

prompt_templates.title: Basic Screenshot Extraction
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner analysis of one UI image
prompt_templates.prompt: Use design-spec-extraction on the attached screenshot. Create a safe project slug and produce the final design specification with layout, colors, typography, and components.

prompt_templates.title: Figma Export Handoff
prompt_templates.scenario: Structured handoff from a design export
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze this Figma export with design-spec-extraction. Focus on design tokens, component hierarchy, spacing, and developer handoff notes.

prompt_templates.title: Accessibility-Focused Review
prompt_templates.prompt: Run design-spec-extraction on this screen and emphasize accessibility. Report contrast issues, focus indicators, touch targets, labels, and recommended fixes.

prompt_templates.title: Multi-State Component Audit
prompt_templates.prompt: Use design-spec-extraction across these default, hover, active, and disabled state images. Compare states and consolidate variants into one component specification.

output_examples.input: A landing page screenshot with hero, cards, and a call to action.
output: Extracted 24 colors with primitive and semantic groupings.
Identified a 12-column desktop grid with 24px gutters.
Cataloged hero, card, navigation, and button components.
Flagged two contrast issues and suggested accessibility fixes.

output_examples.input: A dashboard mockup with sidebar navigation and data cards.
output: Mapped header, sidebar, content regions, and card containers.
Detected typography roles for headings, labels, metrics, and body text.
Extracted spacing and radius tokens for repeated card patterns.

output_examples.input: A set of button state images for a design system.
output: Grouped button variants by primary, secondary, disabled, and focus states.
Recorded visible color, border, shadow, and focus indicator differences.
Produced component notes suitable for implementation review.

best_practices: Use high-resolution, user-authorized images so color and spacing estimates are more reliable.
Use a safe project slug with letters, numbers, and hyphens for output paths.
Provide separate images for hover, focus, disabled, and responsive states when those details matter.
anti_patterns: Do not analyze confidential screens that contain secrets, credentials, or private customer data.
Do not reuse unsanitized project names in shell commands or output paths.
Do not send the final specification into code generation without reviewing estimates and accessibility findings.

faq.question: What inputs does this skill need?
faq.answer: It needs user-provided screenshots, Figma exports, mockups, or approved website captures.

faq.question: Does it capture my screen automatically?
faq.answer: No. It only analyzes visual files or images that the user provides.

faq.question: What does the output include?
faq.answer: The output includes tokens, layout data, component hierarchy, accessibility notes, confidence scores, and recommendations.

faq.question: Can it identify exact fonts and colors?
faq.answer: It estimates them from the image unless the source file provides exact design metadata.

faq.question: Where are files written?
faq.answer: The workflow writes local pass files and a final design specification under a .design-specs project directory.

faq.question: Is the result ready for production?
faq.answer: It is a strong handoff starting point, but teams should review estimates and validate tokens before production use.
